title: Thermo-FL: Thermal-Aware Robust Federated Fine-Tuning of Large Language Models for Edge AI

C-a.quote: On the server side, Thermo-FL introduces TERRA, a robust aggregation pipeline for dynamically sparse LoRA updates that combines norm filtering, mask-aware directional validation, adaptive active-coordinate clipping, and mask-aware aggregation.
C-a.locator: Abstract and Section IV-C; FOUR server-side mechanisms are applied in sequence to the same round and each has its own subsection and its own stated defense purpose. (1) Norm filtering, "a) Robust norm filtering: The first stage of the TERRA pipeline, denoted by Fnorm , enforces a round-adaptive magnitude constraint on the decoded sparse updates."; (2) mask-aware directional validation, whose purpose is stated as "Low or negative alignment indicates that the update is inconsistent with the recent optimization trajectory and may correspond to sign-flipping or poisoning behavior."; (3) adaptive active-coordinate clipping, "c) Adaptive active-coordinate clipping: The third stage of TERRA, denoted by Fclip , bounds the coordinate-level influence of updates that passes through norm filtering and (t) directional validation."; (4) mask-aware aggregation, "d) Mask-aware aggregation: The final stage, Fagg , is responsible for aggregating the clipped sparse updates without treating missing coordinates as zeros.". The pipeline's collective purpose is stated at the end of Section IV, "To sum it up, we have designed the TERRA pipeline to limit the adversarial influence through a sequence of complementary constraints. First of all, Norm filtering removes extrememagnitude updates, followed by mask-aware directional validation reducing sign-flipped or inconsistent updates. Then, adaptive clipping bounds the coordinate-level effect of retained updates, and finally, mask-aware aggregation prevents sparse missingness from being interpreted as zero evidence.", with its scope honestly bounded, "These mechanisms do not replace cryptographic guarantees or fully eliminate Byzantine behavior, but they provide a robust aggregation layer tailored to the sparse LoRA updates produced by Thermo-FL.". AMENDMENT 3 EXCISION: the CLIENT-side thermal control -- "On the client side, Thermo-FL adjusts the active LoRA-layer fraction and transmitted update density as devices heat or cool, reducing workload under thermal stress." -- is NOT counted, because its stated purpose is workload and temperature regulation, not resisting corrupted updates; that is a purpose kind new to the frame and it is recorded in A5's excised list rather than argued

C-b.quote: To sum it up, we have designed the TERRA pipeline to limit the adversarial influence through a sequence of complementary constraints. First of all, Norm filtering removes extrememagnitude updates, followed by mask-aware directional validation reducing sign-flipped or inconsistent updates. Then, adaptive clipping bounds the coordinate-level effect of retained updates, and finally, mask-aware aggregation prevents sparse missingness from being interpreted as zero evidence.
C-b.locator: Section IV-C; this is the most explicit C-b in the frame -- a four-term enumeration in which each constituent is assigned the region of the attack space the previous one leaves open, and the pairwise version is stated separately for the first two stages, "This filter is scale invariant and thus complements norm filtering, as it does 7 not require all retained updates to have similar magnitudes, but it requires the transmitted coordinates to align with the recent accepted update trajectory.", and for the third, "Even after the first two filtering stages of norm and direction filtering, a retained adversarial update may place large values in a small number". The reason is restated as a design conclusion after the experiment, "These results support the design choice of combining norm filtering, mask-aware directional validation, adaptive active-coordinate clipping, and mask-aware aggregation as complementary stages rather than independent alternatives."

C-c.quote: RQ1: Robustness. Does the TERRA pipeline improve the robustness against sign flip and mixed Byzantine attacks when compared with dense and sparse FedAvg-LoRA,
C-c.locator: Section V; the metric is the composed system's ROBUST ACCURACY -- exact-match accuracy on GSM8K and BoolQ measured under a sign-flip/scale Byzantine attack and a mixed attack, plus a physical testbed under sign-flip/scale and MITM noise, "In the Byzantine setting, one client submitted sign-scaled updates with γ = −10. In the MITM setting, Gaussian noise proportional to the update standard deviation was injected into transmitted update" and "We evaluated three configurations: FedAvg-full, which averaged full-density LoRA adapter states with standard FedAvg; Thermo-FL without TERRA, which used thermal-aware client control and sparse transmission with FedAvg-style aggregation; and Thermo-FL, which used thermal-aware control, sparse encoding, and TERRA aggregation.". As on DP-BR-FedAvg, the strings ASR and attack success occur zero times while the referent is present in every reported table

Norm filtering, directional validation, adaptive clipping, and mask-aware aggregation worked together to limit highmagnitude, misaligned, and coordinate-concentrated adversarial updates.
C-e.locator: Section V-A Finding 3; the claim names each constituent and the class of adversarial update it is credited with limiting. coder_note:
A THIRD C-d SHAPE, AND A5 MUST NAME IT BECAUSE THE RUBRIC'S DIRECTION CLAUSE DOES NOT MENTION IT. The frame now has three ways a paper can hold a downstream mechanism fixed while varying what reaches it: REMOVAL of an upstream stage (RKD, STAR-FL), SUBSTITUTION of an upstream rule (FedSAC, Secure-CHG, R2CFL), and CUMULATIVE BUILD-UP, where arms are nested and each adds one upstream filter on top of a fixed downstream aggregation (this row). The build-up is the most informative of the three per unit of compute, because n arms give n-1 nested contrasts all sharing one downstream, and it is the shape our own ladder most resembles apart from the dose being categorical rather than graded. It is also the shape most likely to be MISCODED by a rubric keyed to the word ablation, because the arms read as a feature-addition table for the proposed method rather than as an intervention.

THE UPSTREAM STAGE HERE IS A FUNCTION OF AMBIENT HARDWARE STATE, WHICH IS A GENUINELY NEW STRUCTURAL KIND AND A LIMIT ON EVERY INVARIANCE ASSUMPTION IN THE FRAME. The client-side sparsification density is set by measured device temperature -- "On the client side, Thermo-FL adjusts the active LoRA-layer fraction and transmitted update density as devices heat or cool, reducing workload under thermal stress.", with "The sparse transmission ratio ρ was adjusted between 50% and 1% using a clipped linear policy." -- so the transformation applied upstream of TERRA's filters is determined by an EXOGENOUS variable that no defense controls and that differs between deployments of identical code. Secure-CHG's routing was state-dependent but the state was a measured property of the run (convergence); R2CFL's was closed-loop but endogenous. This is the first row where composition invariance could fail between two runs of the same system in different rooms. A5 should add it to the structural axis as EXOGENOUSLY ROUTED, and A3 can use it in one clause: the upstream stage is not always a design choice.

C-b IS THE STRONGEST IN THE FRAME AND IT IS WORTH QUOTING IN FULL IN THE AUDIT TABLE. Four constituents, each assigned the residue of the one before, in one sentence -- "To sum it up, we have designed the TERRA pipeline to limit the adversarial influence through a sequence of complementary constraints. First of all, Norm filtering removes extrememagnitude updates, followed by mask-aware directional validation reducing sign-flipped or inconsistent updates. Then, adaptive clipping bounds the coordinate-level effect of retained updates, and finally, mask-aware aggregation prevents sparse missingness from being interpreted as zero evidence." -- with the pairwise complementarity argued separately ("This filter is scale invariant and thus complements norm filtering, as it does 7 not require all retained updates to have similar magnitudes, but it requires the transmitted coordinates to align with the recent accepted update trajectory." for directional versus norm, "Even after the first two filtering stages of norm and direction filtering, a retained adversarial update may place large values in a small number" for clipping after both). Against this, our own paper's C-b analogue is thin, and A3 should not imply that defense papers fail to motivate their pairings: they do it well and often. The audit's claim is about what they measure, never about whether they think.

WHAT THE ROW DOES NOT SUPPLY, WHICH IS WHY IT IS DESIGN = YES AND NOT A PRIMARY. It has C-d, so it is not outcome-gated. But note what it still does not do, because A4 needs the distinction: the ablation varies the upstream COMPOSITION (which filters are present) and never varies an upstream stage's SETTING at fixed composition, so there is no dose and no attenuation curve; and no arm substitutes a different downstream aggregator, so like DP-BR-FedAvg it cannot produce an ordering across defenses. Two attacks at one strength each ("In the Byzantine setting, one client submitted sign-scaled updates with γ = −10. In the MITM setting, Gaussian noise proportional to the update standard deviation was injected into transmitted update"), one round reported (round 25), no seeds and no intervals anywhere.

FIRST LLM ROW IN THE FRAME, AND THE SPARSITY COUPLING IS SUBSTANTIVE RATHER THAN COSMETIC. Because updates arrive with heterogeneous support, the downstream aggregation must distinguish a missing coordinate from a transmitted zero, which is why every stage is mask-aware. That makes the upstream stage's effect on the downstream mechanism structural rather than statistical: the upstream stage changes the SUPPORT the downstream statistic is computed over, not merely the values. Our own composition channels (pixel/scaling manipulations feeding coordinate-wise rules) are the statistical case. Worth one sentence in A5's limitations, since our Proposition is stated for a fixed coordinate space.

NUMERIC-BLOCK HAZARD, RESOLVED AND DISCLOSED. Table II extracts as two COLUMN-MAJOR blocks of fifteen numbers (five arms x three attack settings, GSM8K then BoolQ), with no row or column labels interleaved. The mapping is recoverable and I confirmed it against the one value the prose states in words -- the 2.35% collapse of mask-aware aggregation under the mixed attack on GSM8K, quoted under C-d -- and that is the ONLY cell from either block used anywhere in this record. Every other claim about the table rests on the arm names in the caption, which extract cleanly, or on the paper's own prose. This is the same discipline applied on Secure-CHG and STAR-FL.

EXTRACTOR NOTE: coded WITHOUT the extraction aid -- the TENTH such row -- and so contributing no data point to A5's bucket tallies. Vocabulary profile: 0 hits for ASR, 0 for attack success, 1 for backdoor, 2 for ablation, 0 for w/o, 23 for Byzantine, 50 for clip. As on DP-BR-FedAvg, an aid keyed to backdoor vocabulary would have judged this a hardware paper; it carries four defense-purposed mechanisms, an explicit complementarity argument and a nested ablation.
